source_read: PDF PDFs/Ketamine/Newcomer_1999_NMDAHypofunctionModel.pdf, printed pp. 106-118 (text pp. 106-115 read in full; references skimmed). Born-digital text layer whose symbol font prints = as 5, +/- as 6 and minus as 2; pp. 111-114 rendered at 150 dpi and every number used checked there (Figures 1-6, Tables 1-2, the recall sentence on p. 112).

claims.overstatement: Minor. 'Held at measured steady blood levels for 2 hours': plasma ketamine was sampled at 20, 60 and 120 min, peaked at 20 min and was stable at 60 and 120 min; steady state 'by 30 minutes' is the authors' calculation, and the low condition was below the assay limit, so steady levels were shown for the two larger conditions from about 30 to 120 min (the maintenance infusion ran about 2 hours). Measured steady levels (about 88 and 16-18 ng/mL, read from Figure 6) were well under the targeted 150 and 45 ng/mL. The claim's opening ('recover within about an hour or two of the end of the infusion') gets no support from this source: cognition was tested only during the steady state, never after the infusion. 'Fell with the condition' is fair for the omnibus test; the paper's step-by-step comparisons are one-tailed (see note), so 'at and below concentrations producing other symptoms' (the authors' phrase) should not be repeated from it.
claims.note: Numbers checked (born-digital text with a symbol font that prints = as 5, +/- as 6 and minus as 2; each value was checked on the rendered page): F(3,41) = 5.11, p = 0.004; immediate F(3,41) = 3.92, p = 0.02; delayed F(3,41) = 5.03, p = 0.005; 21.2 (rendered page shows 21.2, not -1.2); 18.6%; DMS F(3,40) = 2.93, p = 0.045. Editors' calculation of the 18.6%: 21.2 / 0.186 = 114, matching the placebo bar of about 114 bits in Figure 4, so the percentage recomputes. Every paired t test p value in the paper matches a one-tailed test, which is not stated: placebo against low t(14) = 2.02 printed p = 0.03 (two-tailed .063), placebo against moderate t(14) = 2.47 printed 0.01 (two-tailed .027), placebo against high t(13) = 3.30 printed 0.003 (two-tailed .006). The non-verbal (DMS) effect was significant only in the univariate ANOVA, not in the multivariate one, and its post hoc tests rest on t(5) and t(7), i.e. 6 and 8 people; 'preliminary' in the magnitude is apt.

anchors.extracted: 15 healthy men aged 18-40 (mean 21.7, SD 3.2) recruited by local advertisement; excluded: Axis I or Cluster A Axis II disorder, any substance use disorder in the past 12 months, any past use of PCP or ketamine. Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized, within-person comparison of saline and 3 fixed steady-state intravenous conditions on 4 non-consecutive mornings (mean 2.6, SD 1.1, days apart); blinded clinical and cognitive assessment during each infusion, abbreviated assessments before, 60 min after the infusion and about 48 hours later.

anchors.locator: Methods › Ketamine Dosing and Safety Considerations; Analysis
anchors.extracted: Study conditions: loading doses of 0.27, 0.081 and 0.0243 mg/kg over 10 min, then 0.00225, 0.000675 and 0.0002025 mg/kg/min, targeting steady plasma levels of 150, 45 and 13.5 ng/mL; highest total 0.54 mg/kg over the session (0.27 + 0.00225 x 120 min). Paragraph recall and DMS analysed with an added factor for task condition; significant omnibus effects followed by paired t tests across dose levels; univariate ANOVAs used when data points were missing.

Plasma ketamine peaked at the 20-min sample and was stable at 60 and 120 min in the moderate and high conditions; low-condition levels were below the assay limit. Steady state 'by 30 minutes' was calculated from the 20- and 60-min levels and half-lives. Figure 6 (read from the plot): high about 108 ng/mL at 20 min, about 88 at 60 and 120 min; moderate about 27, 18 and 16 ng/mL; assay threshold about 10 ng/mL. Condition x time F(9,125) = 73.62, p = 0.0001.

anchors.locator: Results › Cognitive Results › Paragraph Recall; Figure 4
anchors.extracted: Two recorded narratives of 44 information units each, immediate and 30-min delayed recall (task described pp. 108-109). Main effect of condition on total recall F(3,41) = 5.11, p = 0.004; recall condition F(1,14) = 46.14; no condition x recall-condition interaction; immediate F(3,41) = 3.92, p = 0.02; delayed F(3,41) = 5.03, p = 0.005. Mean fall in total correct recall from placebo to the high condition 21.2, stated as an 18.6% decrease. Figure 4 (read from the plot, mean bits recalled): placebo about 114, low about 102.5, moderate about 103, high about 93; placebo vs high t(13) = 3.30, p = 0.003; vs moderate t(14) = 2.47, p = 0.01; vs low t(14) = 2.02, p = 0.03; low vs high t(13) = 1.70, p = 0.06; moderate vs high t(13) = 1.57, p = 0.07 (all printed p values are one-tailed by recomputation).

anchors.locator: Results › Cognitive Results › DMS (continues at top of p. 112 right column); Figure 5 (p. 113)
anchors.extracted: Non-verbal delayed match-to-sample: condition F(3,40) = 2.93, p = 0.045 in the univariate ANOVA, not significant in the multivariate analysis that required complete data; Figure 5 ratios about 1.34 (placebo), 1.43 (low), 1.32 (moderate), 1.15 (high); placebo vs high t(5) = 2.04, p = 0.05 and low vs high t(7) = 2.78, p = 0.01, i.e. 6 and 8 people with complete pairs.

anchors.locator: Results › Cognitive Results › Other Cognitive Tasks
anchors.extracted: No effect of condition, with adjusted or unadjusted p values, on the modified Stroop task, the continuous performance task, verbal fluency or the spatial delayed response task.

anchors.locator: Results › Additional Clinical and Adverse Events, and Safety Measures (paragraph continued from p. 112); Results › Plasma Results (right column of p. 113)
anchors.extracted: Covarying rated drowsiness, and plasma epinephrine, norepinephrine, glucose and cortisol from the nearest time point, left no main effect or interaction with condition for paragraph recall or DMS.

The authors note that no similar effect appeared on the 120-s delay of the spatial task, attribute this to differences in task sensitivity or difficulty, and state that psychometric differences in the sensitivity of the tasks could contribute to the apparent selectivity of the memory effect; higher doses or testing during loading might show effects on other functions.

claims.overstatement: None for the Newcomer sentence. Two qualifiers a reader needs: the BPRS 'hallucinatory behavior' item, part of the positive subscale, was deliberately scored to include perceptual distortions as well as hallucinations (pp. 108-109), and the authors detected no formal thought disorder or language disorganization apart from modest alogia changes (p. 114). 'Abbreviated, unblinded check about 48 hours later' is a fair reading: the paper calls the pre- and post-infusion abbreviated assessments unblinded and lists the 48-hour one among the abbreviated assessments (p. 108).
claims.note: Checked on the rendered pages: BPRS positive F(3,42) = 21.84, p < 0.0001 (Figure 2, p. 111); SANS total F(3,42) = 10.55, p < 0.0001 (Figure 3); BPRS negative F(3,42) = 2.89, p = 0.047 (p. 111). All as printed; recomputed p for F(3,42) = 2.89 is .047. For the claim's opening sentence: Figure 1 shows BPRS totals back at baseline (about 19) at the post-washout rating 60 min after the infusion in every condition, from about 23.3 during the high condition (read from the plot); that rating was the abbreviated, unblinded one. For the blinding sentence: nausea in 6 people at the high condition and 1 at the moderate, with 2 vomiting, and one person unable to finish testing (pp. 112-113); no blinding check is reported.

anchors.locator: Results › Behavioral Results, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Figure 1
anchors.extracted: Mild dose-dependent positive and negative schizophrenia-like symptoms. BPRS total across baseline, infusion and post-washout: condition x time F(6,83) = 17.62, p = 0.0001; positive subscale interaction F(6,83) = 22.54, p = 0.0001; negative subscale F(6,83) = 2.73, p = 0.02. Blinded ratings during steady state: BPRS total F(3,42) = 21.60, p = 0.0001. Figure 1 (read from the plot): BPRS total about 19.5 at baseline in all conditions, about 23.3 (high), 20.2 (moderate), 19.2 (low and placebo) during the infusion, and about 18.7-19.0 in every condition at washout.

anchors.locator: Results › Behavioral Results › Positive Symptoms; Negative Symptoms; Figures 2 and 3
anchors.extracted: BPRS positive subscale (hallucinatory behavior, conceptual disorganization, unusual thought content) F(3,42) = 21.84, p < 0.0001; Figure 2 about 3.0 (floor) for placebo and low, about 3.4 moderate, about 5.1 high. BPRS negative subscale F(3,42) = 2.89, p = 0.047 (placebo vs high t(14) = -1.95, p = 0.04, one-tailed by recomputation; two-tailed .07). SANS total F(3,42) = 10.55, p < 0.0001; Figure 3 about 1.6, 1.3, 2.9 and 7.7; placebo vs high t(14) = 4.44, p = 0.0003. Participants' remarks at the high condition describe visual distortions (own hand looking small, a shadow passing a window).

SANS subscales, mean (SD), placebo to high: affective flattening 0.2 (0.6) to 1.4 (2.1), F(3,42) = 4.49, p = 0.008; alogia 0.0 to 0.6, F = 2.51, p = 0.07; avolition-apathy 0.2 to 1.5, F = 9.08, p = 0.0001; anhedonia-asociality 0.3 to 2.9, F = 6.51, p = 0.001; attention 0.9 to 1.3, F = 2.61, p = 0.06. BPRS anxiety-depression F(3,42) = 5.73, p = 0.002, from somatic concern. The authors call the syndrome mild in intensity, with participants comfortable, alert and oriented, and report no persistent abnormal symptoms at the 48-hour post-infusion assessment.

Full clinical battery (BPRS, SANS, a 5-point Clinical & Adverse Events Checklist) rated blind to condition during the infusion; abbreviated, unblinded BPRS and checklist ratings before and after each infusion; abbreviated assessments also about 48 hours after. The BPRS hallucinatory-behavior item was scored so that perceptual distortions as well as hallucinations counted.

anchors.locator: Results › Additional Clinical and Adverse Events, and Safety Measures
anchors.extracted: Transient blood-pressure rises; nausea in 6 people at the high condition and 1 at the moderate, 2 vomiting; one person with nausea could not complete testing. During loading, dose-related drowsiness, difficulty concentrating, dizziness, confusion, 'high', floating sensations, 'dream-like state' and altered sense of time at moderate levels or below; during steady state the same at mild levels or below. No blinding check reported.

Effects described as mild, well tolerated and without detectable residual effects; no formal thought disorder or language disorganization detected at the steady-state conditions apart from modest SANS alogia effects, though blocking, loosening of associations and language disorganization were noted during the loading doses.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall high agreed for the clinician-rated symptom outcomes. By RoB 2's signalling questions, probable awareness without deviations gives 'some concerns' in domain 2; the 'high' belongs in domain 4 for the BPRS and SANS (raters probably unblinded by nausea, vomiting and visible effects, and outcome open to influence). For the objective memory tasks 'some concerns' would be defensible, so a claim resting on paragraph recall alone is less affected.

interpretation_gap.note: I would rate it moderate, not minor: the abstract's headline conclusion (memory affected at or below the concentrations producing other symptoms; memory impairment occurring first, followed by other symptoms) rests on one paired comparison that is one-tailed without saying so (placebo against low recall, two-tailed p = .063) at a concentration below the assay limit, and the conditions are labelled by targets (150/45/13.5 ng/mL) that were not reached. The card's own 'claimed' text documents all of this; only the label is in question.

missed: outcomes.assessor_blinding says 'vomiting in 2 at the moderate dose'; the paper (pp. 112-113) gives 6 with nausea at the high condition and 1 at the moderate, 'with 2 subjects vomiting' without naming the condition (and with only one person nauseated at the moderate condition, 2 vomiting there is unlikely). KF11 and the risk-of-bias note have it right; the outcomes field should match.

The baseline and post-washout BPRS ratings (Figure 1) were the abbreviated unblinded ones (p. 108); the return to baseline 60 minutes after the infusion therefore rests on unblinded ratings, which matters for any claim that the symptoms pass within an hour or two.
Cognition was tested only during the steady-state infusion; there is no post-infusion or 48-hour cognitive test, so this source says nothing about how quickly the memory effect resolves.
